info.title: Campbooks admin API
info.description: Instance administration. Every operation answers 404 (as for a route that does not exist) unless the caller is a user whose bearer token carries the `admin:access` scope and whose admin profile grants the operation's permission (`x-campbooks-admin.permission`; `super` grants all). Then a token whose last sign-in (`auth_time`) is more than an hour old answers 401 `admin_reauth_required`. Every request past the profile check is recorded in the audit trail. Calls are rate-limited per caller (429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`). These operations are not part of the operation catalogue (`/openapi.json`): automation and the assistant cannot call them. Admin profiles are managed only with the server's CLI (`campbooks-server admin`), never over HTTP. The web app reaches this API through `/bff/admin/*`.

last_used_at.description: When it was last used to sign in.

AdminWorkspace.description: A workspace, as an administrator sees it.

deleted_at.description: When it was deleted (it is purged later); absent while it lives.

AdminWorkspaceDetail.description: A workspace and who is in it.

members.description: Its members, in the order they joined.

pending_invitations.description: How many invitations are pending (not accepted, not expired).

next.description: The `after` of the next page; absent on the last one.

AiAnswersCheck.description:
How the `decide` model did on its answers check (eight fictional emails
whose answers are not in doubt). While it does not pass, the model's
answers are not used: the inbox is sorted by the rules alone.

right.description: Expected answers the model got right, once a check finished.

total.description: Expected answers asked, once a check finished.

AiLocation.description: Where an AI role's endpoint is, as far as mail content is concerned.

AiRoleStatus.description:
One AI role, without a secret: the provider is shown as scheme, host
and port only, and keys never.

oneOf.description:
The `decide` role's answers check: whether the model gets obvious
fictional emails right. `null` for the other roles, and when the
role is not configured or may not receive mail.

configured.description: Whether a provider is configured for it.

content_allowed.description:
Whether it may receive mail content: on the instance's network, or
opted in with `CAMPBOOKS_AI__<ROLE>__EXTERNAL_CONTENT=allow`. When
`false`, nothing calls it with content (the decide pass leaves
sorting to rules); only the reachability probe runs.

endpoint.description: The provider's scheme, host and port.

oneOf.description: Whether its endpoint is on the instance's network.

reachable.description:
Whether the provider answered a probe within 3 seconds (probes are
reused for a minute); `null` when not configured.

AiUsageDay.description: A day's AI usage across the instance.

cap.description:
Model calls a workspace may make per UTC day
(`CAMPBOOKS_AI__DAILY_CALLS_PER_WORKSPACE`); `null` when there is no
cap.

reserve.description:
Calls of the cap kept for what people ask themselves (the
assistant): background work, such as reading new mail, stops this
many calls short of the cap. `null` when there is no cap.

resets_at.description: When that day's counts start again: 00:00 UTC the next day.

workspaces.description:
The workspaces that used AI that day: those the cap refused first,
then by calls.

AiUse.description: Calls of one role for one feature.

failed.description: Of which failed (no answer, or an unusable one).

prompt_tokens.description: Prompt tokens the providers reported (0 when they report none).

BlobBackend.description: Which object store holds the blobs.

Capability.description: What a connection lets Campbooks do with the account.

CodeState.description: What a signup code can still do.

exports_telemetry.description: Whether traces and metrics are exported over OTLP.

latency_ms.description: How long a trivial query took, in milliseconds.

migrations_applied.description: How many schema migrations are applied.

mail_providers.description: The mail providers mailboxes can be connected from (`google`, …).

sign_in_providers.description: The providers people can sign in with (`google`, …).

last_error.description: The last failure, truncated; never carries secrets.

workspace_id.description: The workspace it belongs to; `null` for instance-wide work.

FailedPage.description: A page of dead jobs, newest first.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

IdentityProvider.description: Which identity provider issues this instance's tokens (ADR 0014).

JobAction.description: The result of acting on one job.

KindSummary.description: The jobs of one kind on one queue.

expired_leases.description:
Running, but past its lease: the worker stopped renewing it and the
next upkeep hands it back.

failed.description: Dead: out of attempts, or failed for good. Kept for inspection.

oldest_ready_seconds.description: Age of the oldest ready job of this kind, in seconds.

ready.description: Pending and due now: waiting for a worker.

scheduled.description: Pending for later: new delayed work, or waiting out a retry backoff.

display_name.description: Their name, as their identity provider gives it.

email.description:
Their email address, as their identity provider gives it, when it
verified it (an unverified address is never shown: anyone can claim
one).

you.description: It is the caller (by user id, never by email).

expires_at.description:
After this it cannot be redeemed; must be in the future. Never
expires when absent.

label.description: What it is for (who it goes to), 1 to 100 characters.

max_uses.description: How many times it can be redeemed: 1 to 100000, default 1.

code.description: The code to hand over, like `K7QM-2XWP-9DHE-RT4A`. Shown here once.

entry.description: The stored code (without the code itself).

Outcome.description: What a retry or discard did.

Phase.description: Where a stream is in its reading.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable reason (`not_found`, `invalid_token`,
`last_owner`, …); the same in every locale. Match on this, never on
`title` or `detail`.

detail.description: What went wrong in this occurrence, in the request's locale.

title.description:
Short summary of the problem type, in the request's locale
(`Content-Language`).

type.description:
URI identifying the problem type; `about:blank` when the HTTP status
says it all.

example.detail: This resource does not exist, or you cannot see it.
example.title: Not found

QueueSummary.description:
The queue at a glance: one row per queue and kind with unfinished or
failed work. Succeeded jobs are pruned and not counted.

kinds.description: Counts per queue and kind, sorted by queue then kind.

oldest_ready_seconds.description: Age of the oldest job that is ready to run and waiting, in seconds.

watched.description:
The dead jobs of the kinds an operator must hear about, by what they
are for (each kind's `Watch`), sorted by code; every watched code is
listed, with 0 when nothing died.

RejectSignupRequest.description: Why a request is turned down.

reason.description:
An optional note for the administrators' records, at most 500
characters. The requester is told only that they were not approved.

RequestStatus.description: Where a user's signup request stands.

RetryKindResult.description: How many jobs a bulk retry requeued.

more.description:
Whether the batch limit was reached, so more dead jobs of the kind
may remain: call again.

requeued.description: Jobs put back on their queue.

Role.description: A member's role in a workspace.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

SignupCodeView.description:
One minted signup code. The code itself is never here: only its
administrators saw it, once, when it was minted.

created_by.description: The administrator who minted it (their account id).

expires_at.description: After this it cannot be redeemed.

max_uses.description: How many times it can be redeemed.

SignupPolicy.description: Who may create a workspace when they are not a member of any yet.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

requests.description: The requests: pending first, then newest first.

SignupRequestView.description:
One signup request, as an administrator sees it: who asked and where it
stands. No content, only the account's own name and address.

display_name.description: Their display name, when their sign-in carried one.

email.description: Their email address, when their sign-in carried one.

reason.description: Why it was turned down, when the administrator said.

user_id.description: The requesting user (also the request's id).

WatchedSummary.description: The dead jobs of the kinds watched under one code.

code.description:
What the kinds are for (`suspension_fanout`: a suspension, or its
lift, reaching the rules a member taught); the client words it.

failed.description:
How many of their jobs are dead: until each is retried, what it
carried has not happened.

kinds.description: The kinds watched under it, sorted.

WorkspaceAiUsage.description: One workspace's AI usage on the day.

capped.description: Whether the cap refused any of its calls that day.

capped_at.description: The first refusal, when there was one.

remaining.description:
Calls left today, the reserve included; `null` for another day or
without a cap.

uses.description: Its calls by role and feature.

admin.description: An OAuth 2.1 access token for a person (not a client), issued to one of Campbooks' own apps with the `admin:access` scope, whose account has an admin profile.
